newsitem.title: TANZANIA: UN Rwanda tribunal delays hearing of top suspect.
newsitem.headline: UN Rwanda tribunal delays hearing of top suspect.

text.p: A U.N. tribunal postponed on Thursday the first hearing on its most prominent suspect Theoneste Bagosora after his defence lawyer failed to appear in court.
The initial hearing for Bagosora, 56, cabinet director in Rwanda's former defence ministry, was delayed until March 7, presiding judge William Sekule of Tanzania told the court.
Bagosora looked confident as he was brought under guard into the Arusha courtroom wearing a dark blue suit and glasses.
"Your honour I am ready to begin right away," he told Sekule, before adding that he wanted to switch defence lawyers to Luc de Temmerman of Belgium.

Bagosora, who faces a maximum sentence of life imprisonment if found guilty, assumed de facto control of events in Rwanda in the first few days of the genocide, according to the prosecution indictment.
The court heard on Thursday that defence counsel Benjamin Ondigui of Cameroon was absent because he missed a flight.
"Yesterday evening Ondigui sent a fax to the tribunal saying he had missed his flight and that he was going to reroute his trip again through Nairobi," a registry official told the court.
"The initial hearing of Theoneste Bagosora has been postponed until March 7," Sekule told the court.

Andre Ntagerura, a former Rwandan transport minister , appeared after Bagosora and pleaded not guilty to six counts of genocide, crimes against humanity and violations of Article Three of the Geneva Convention.
Ntagerura, 47, is accused of allowing government vehicles and specifically buses to transport Hutu extremist Interahamwe militia and weapons in southwest Cyangugu province during the genocide.

An estimated 800,000 members of the Tutsi minority and Hutu political moderates were slaughtered between April and July 1994 by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs following the killing of Rwanda's Hutu president.

This week's appearances by four suspects follow a scathing U.N. report into activities of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR), set up in November 1994 but dogged by delays. The report detailed gross mismanagement and financial incompetence.

Bagosora was brought from Cameroon for trial with four other indicted genocide suspects last month. The two other suspects pleaded not guilty to genocide and crimes against humanity in their first appearances in the Arusha court on Wednesday.
